title: IntentFix: Automated Logic Vulnerability Repair via LLM-Driven Intent Modeling
summary: The original IntentFix framework repairs logic vulnerabilities with a multi-phase, intent-centric pipeline: it extracts an explicit model of developer intent, detects the semantic gap and attack vector, then generates and verifies a patch. RQ1 compares it against zero-shot and Chain-of-Thought LLM baselines on 1,107 real-world logic-vulnerability CVEs.

This reproduction replaces the pipeline with a single Claude call under two prompts -- Prompt A (black-box) and Prompt B (informed) -- generated from the paper. Each call receives the vulnerable code and a high-level CWE description (section 4.3); an AI oracle then scores patch correctness given the vulnerable code, the generated patch, the ground-truth fix, and the CWE description (section 4.4.1).

dataset.name: IntentFix Logic-Vulnerability Pairs (CWE-840 family)
dataset.note: Built by utils/produce_dataset.py from the upstream artifact, with the CWE description attached from the MITRE CWE API. Heavily skewed (CWE-770 = 72.6%). pair_0010 and pair_1011 are held out as few-shot examples (dataset/heldout_fewshot_ids.json).

original_result.note: From Table 2 / section 5.1.1. Paper reports both AI-oracle and manual-validation accuracy.
